evidence: The only eager read goes through /proc/self/fd/N of the handle whose footer was checked (spy on pq.read_table).
A larger replacement after admission is rejected 'not read', with zero read_table calls.
A replacement with the same footer (same shape, other values) is read within the admitted size, then rejected by the hash of the same handle.
A file renamed over the input during the read: the read and hash see the original inode (consistent), and the later copy check rejects the new path ('changed during release creation').
fd reuse: the fd stays open across footer check, read and hash in one thread, and the /proc magic link reopens the same inode, so no fd reuse window exists.
Native Windows (no /proc) keeps the documented identity-check-to-read window.

checks.evidence: The manifest records declared_by_contributor ['converter', 'review'] and keeps the review verbatim. The card says 'declared by the contributor' and 'The builder did not verify this review', and states the scope or 'not declared'. It uses no 'approved', 'certified' or 'verified review' wording. Adjacent, G2 territory: the card line 'Profile review status: reviewed' is the profile's own label and is not marked as declared. Labelling it 'declared in the profile' costs nothing and would not enact any G2 option.

evidence: A reviewed or approved profile is refused before any read when applicability is {} or absent for any task. That covers a single task and a two-task profile with one task missing; zero read_table calls.
Malformed applicability (a list) fails closed with CLI exit 2.
A legacy profile with no status and no applicability still releases with the legacy limitation.

Residual R2 (low; convention): the check needs only a nonempty block. The worker's fixtures use 'applicability: {task: [level_walking]}', which restricts by task only and says nothing about population or condition, yet satisfies the rule. A real profile could do the same.
Follow-up: require at least one key other than task/task_id, or name the required keys (for example population), in the same logged default as G2.

The repo already has one convention for review records: provenance review requires reviewer and a timezone-stamped reviewed_at, and scope is optional but labelled (G3, verified here). Applying the same rule to profiles marked reviewed or approved is consistency, not a new convention.
This is the conservative direction AGENTS.md asks for: a bare label is not evidence, and draft profiles are not release profiles. CORE-01's verifier made the same call for applicability.
It refuses nothing that exists (no committed range profile declares review_status), removes no data, changes no release scope, is reversible, and every release still needs José's approval.
Option A is less conservative than existing practice. Option C adds a requirement not imposed on source reviews; José can opt into it later.
